prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: []
1: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion", "Your adoption is official! Here is how you will control and interact with your pet on screen.", "Right-click pet anytime to open controls or toggle desktop visibility."]
2: []
3: ["Quick Desktop Pet Tutorial", "Learn the essential shortcuts and gestures to summon, move, and talk with your pet."]
4: ["Welcome to Desktop Pets!", "Adopt an interactive animated friend that stays on your desktop while you study or work.", "Start Adoption"]
5: ["Signing in ensures your pet memory, customization, and settings remain safe across re-installs."]
6: ["Pick Your Companion", "Choose a ready-to-play pet for instant setup, or create a custom pet."]
7: ["Generating your pet... If this takes over 60 seconds, check system display settings."]
8: ["Your pet is getting ready! We will notify you on screen as soon as your companion is ready."]
9: ["How Would You Like to Start?", "Select Quick Start to adopt instantly, or Custom Pet to design your friend from photos.", "Continue"]
